---
name: make-music
description: "Compose or revise music, critique mixes against references, and find local samples."
applications:
  - id: ableton
    role: alternative
  - id: logic-pro
    role: alternative
  - id: moda
    role: alternative
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: none
---

## Give the music a reason to stay

Left to its defaults, music becomes a genre label, a repeating chord loop and more layers at
the chorus. Refuse that. You are the best composer on this job, and the bar is a piece people
remember. Find the musical idea that carries the feeling: a rhythmic signature, a melodic
gesture, a texture with character. Give it room to establish itself, develop and return
changed. Let groove, voicing, silence and contrast do the expressive work; adding instruments
is only one way to build energy. A video score should give the picture shape and leave speech
room to breathe. Judge the structure against the brief and references, and use the user's
listening feedback to push the next revision further. If the piece could run indefinitely
without anyone noticing where it starts or ends, give it an arc and an ending that earns its
place.

A beat or part in the user's Ableton Live set follows `ableton-live`. You cannot hear; the user judges by ear.

## Route

Engine commands below are subcommands of the audio engine's CLI that `<voyager_environment>` names.

- Compose in Voyager's audio engine by default when `<voyager_environment>` lists it as ready, video scores included.
- Render each revision to a new versioned WAV; the same .vdaw keeps its history.
- Tweaks ("punchier", "darker", "slower", "less busy", "longer intro"): keep editing the same .vdaw.
- When you composed in the engine, link its .vdaw project in your reply beside the audio, so the user can open it.
- Generate without an engine draft for vocals or lyrics, realistic acoustic or orchestral sound, when the user asks for AI generation or names a provider, and when the audio engine is not ready.
- To change a generated track, split it into stems in an engine project (`track separate FILE`: vocals, drums, bass and other) and edit those instead of regenerating.
- For lyric timings from an existing song, follow [local lyric transcription](../edit-video/SKILL.md#review-footage-locally).

## Critique a track or mix

Requires the audio engine to be ready in `<voyager_environment>`. Report measurements, not a verdict on taste. Without references, `--profile NAME` (`library reference profile list`) gives only a rough genre baseline.

```sh
analyze compare references BOUNCE.wav --reference REF.wav --reference REF2.wav
analyze compare references BOUNCE.wav --reference REFS_DIR --range drop
analyze compare diff --previous OLD.wav NEW.wav
```

For requested changes to an Ableton set, use [ableton-live](../ableton-live/SKILL.md).

## Find local samples

Requires the audio engine to be ready in `<voyager_environment>`. Register sample folders once, then index:

```sh
library path add ~/Splice
library index --no-plugins
```

`sound find --source sample --class snare --want punchy,tight --key "F#m" --folder DIR` searches by sound. `--reference FILE` ranks by similarity; `--more` and `--less` describe changes relative to it. `sound classes` and `sound descriptors` list valid values.

`kit add --name NAME --want dusty,warm --folder DIR` builds a kit from the library. Import picks into a .vdaw with `import audio FILE --track NAME`; for an Ableton set, use [ableton-live](../ableton-live/SKILL.md). For recorded sounds missing from the library, see [Freesound](../make-sound/SKILL.md#sound-effects).

## Generate

When the user explicitly chooses another tool or website, such as Suno on their own custom connector, generate there instead of the credit check and `eleven-music` below; the other rules here still apply.

Otherwise estimate first (`voyager models estimate eleven-music --prompt "..." --count N --json`). Read `voyager models show eleven-music --json` for version selection and route constraints; use the estimate's payer for the actual request. On `no_paying_route`, or `short` with no Voyager plan, say in one line that this shortcut needs Voyager credits or the user's own ElevenLabs key (Connectors → Providers), submit nothing, and offer the audio engine when it is ready and can do the job.

Generate with `eleven-music` through `voyager`: `voyager models run --input - --json` with `{"model": "eleven-music", "prompt": "…", "parameters": {"duration": 10, "instrumental": true}}` (a video's bed is instrumental, the picture's length). Never ask for a particular song's melody or hook. Before generating, read the model's section in [Music models](#music-models). Another music model only when the user names one or needs what Eleven Music lacks (`voyager models list --query "music" --json`). A refused generation of music the user asked for is a billing refusal under the runtime instructions’ paid generation policy. A default bed they didn't ask for never stops the piece: on a billing wall, deliver without it and say so in one line.

## Music models

Eleven Music is the default for songs and instrumental beds. Lyria suits structured musical timing, and MiniMax Music suits lyrics with section tags and a structured prompt.

For a model the user names or an unusual job, `voyager models list --query "music" --json` covers the long tail. `voyager models show MODEL --json` answers inputs and limits, `voyager models estimate` answers price, speed and payer, and `voyager models docs MODEL --json` supplies vendor documentation for fal endpoints.

Exact cue timing is never guaranteed: fit it in the mix.

### Eleven Music (`eleven-music`)

- Use `voyager models show eleven-music --json` for model IDs, parameters and vendor guidance; estimate the request to name its payer. A native `input` uses `duration_seconds` and `model_params.force_instrumental` instead of the shortcut’s `parameters.duration` and `parameters.instrumental`; optional `model_params.model_id` selects the native version.
- BPM holds exactly; key usually.
- Narrate the arrangement with *start with / just / then / bring in*. Without *just*, the model fills the silence.
- A loop is an exclusion: bars, BPM, key and what is banned ("no melody — just drums").
- The shortcut's `parameters.instrumental` defaults to true, so it makes no vocals unless told otherwise. For a song set it false and place the vocals with timing cues: "lyrics begin at 15 seconds",
  "instrumental only after 1:45".

### Lyria 3.5 (`google/lyria-3.5`) and Lyria 3 clip (`fal-ai/lyria3`, `fal-ai/lyria3/pro`)

- The clip model (`fal-ai/lyria3`) always returns 30 s whatever the prompt asks; use Pro (`fal-ai/lyria3/pro`) for longer tracks. `voyager models show fal-ai/lyria3 --json` lists their inputs. Direct length, structure and exclusions in the prompt; on 3.5 write the length ("a 2-minute track").
- Structure as `[Intro] -> [Verse 1] -> [Chorus]` or timestamps: `[0:00-0:15] Intro: …`, "the chorus kicks in at 22 seconds".
- Own lyrics go under `Lyrics:` with section tags; `(moving on)` marks backing vocals. Vocals are default: write "Instrumental only".
- Named artists' voices and copyrighted lyrics are refused.

### MiniMax Music 3 (`minimax/music-3`)

- `prompt` is a structured caption: global metadata (genre, BPM, key, emotional arc, production),
  vocals (gender, timbre, harmonies) and arrangement (instruments per section, groove, space).
- `lyrics` is required. Section tags `[intro] [verse] [pre-chorus] [chorus] [post-chorus] [bridge]
  [instrumental] [solo] [outro]` each go on their own line: text after a tag on the same line is dropped.
- `duration` is a ceiling; size the lyrics to it and read the actual length from the output.

### Stable Audio 2.5

For instrumental textures, see [Stable Audio 2.5](../make-sound/SKILL.md#stable-audio-25).

## Score a video

- With the voiceover in hand, bring it into the score (`import audio VO.wav --track vo`) and duck the music under it there (`bus duck --on BUS --from vo`).
- A generated bed: write the reveal and logo times into the prompt or composition plan as section changes ("open up at 0:12, end on a clean button at 0:30"). Timing is approximate (the job's `audioLength` gives the real length): then shift, trim and fade the bed in the mix so the hit lands on the reveal and the ending lands on the last frame.

Sound effects, the final mix and delivery: [make-sound](../make-sound/SKILL.md#mix-to-the-destination).

## Logic Pro

Logic has no scripting API: write parts as MIDI files and work Logic's menus with computer control.

- A new project: `open -a "Logic Pro" part.mid`, with no file dialog.
- A part for an open project: File > Import > MIDI File, typing the path after Cmd+Shift+G. Never open the browser's All Files tab; it can hang Logic.
- Give every melodic channel a program change so it lands on a software instrument. Channel-10 drums always land on a silent External MIDI track: move the region onto a software instrument track with a drum kit.
- Before a bounce, turn the metronome off (Logic bounces the click), choose WAVE and set the range to the music.

## Asset Sources

`voyager assets search <words> [--type texture|hdri|model|icon|music|pack] [--source …]` and
`voyager assets download <source>:<id> [--resolution 2k]` cover Poly Haven, ambientCG and Kenney
(CC0), game-icons.net and Incompetech; downloads land in `assets/<source>/<id>/` with a receipt
and a `CREDITS` line. An asset you get another way gets the same by hand: `<asset-id>.json`
beside its files (`source`, `id`, `title`, `url`, `authors`, `license`, `licenseUrl`,
`attribution`, `acquiredAt`, `files`) and a `CREDITS` line (title, author, source URL, licence).

- Tell users Poly Haven assets come from Poly Haven. Kenney search matches pack names only.
- game-icons.net is CC BY 3.0, credited per icon author; Incompetech is CC BY 4.0 with Kevin
  MacLeod's credit text, single tracks only.
- Lospec palettes: `https://lospec.com/palette-list/<slug>.json`; credit "<palette> by <author>
  (Lospec)", taking the author from the page when the JSON's is empty.
- Godot Asset Library (plugins and scripts, not art):
  `godotengine.org/asset-library/api/asset?filter=…&godot_version=4.3` (nothing without
  `godot_version`); `cost` is the licence, `/asset/<id>` gives `download_url`.
- OpenGameArt has no API: search pages only, 10 s crawl delay, `/search/` disallowed; licences
  per page.
- Mixamo and itch.io: the user downloads in their own browser (Mixamo's terms forbid other
  access, and its assets aren't redistributable raw; itch.io has no public API).
